doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

chapter: Jazz parties, Metropole and San Diego
title: Collecting records and meeting musicians at Dick Gibson's jazz parties
summary: He met musicians through Gibson's parties from the early 1960s and values their loyal friendship.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well I can tell from your record collection that you must have been collecting all those years.
Yeah, somewhat. But mostly after the law school and so on, that’s when I really picked up on it. Because while I was in the Navy and here I didn’t have any time to do it. But I did then, yes.

What were the years when you first started to meet these musicians? Because I’ve been really amazed over the years how many of them you’ve gotten to know and how did that come about, from your travel?

Jazz parties. I would say in the early 60s it started. I started out I went to — well I knew some people just from rolling around town in San Diego. But I really met them at Dick Gibson’s parties. And I went to 25 of those straight. And I went for the same reason that I wanted to do the archive, I knew that the following year there would be some I wouldn’t see again. And that was true every year. And anyway I went to those parties and Dick and I became very friendly and I went to some of his private parties and so on and I got to know a lot of these people. And some of them I became very friendly with and some of them are just nodding acquaintances. I have found them as a group to be tremendous friends, very loyal. My definition of a friend is a guy you can call at 3 A.M. and say I’m in jail come get me out. And they all would, the ones that I know. So they’ve been almost my best friends all these years. A lot of them.
